clue.text: Society member in black suit

blocks.note: first meaning: an association of people who meet for a shared interest
second meaning: a playing card belonging to one of the two dark suits in the pack

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a club member dressed in a black suit; instead the second half describes a single playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an organised society of members and one playing card of the suit marked with black trefoils.

clue.text: Saved, source of water and wine

blocks.note: a spa is a mineral spring, where healing water rises
red is a colour of wine, used to mean the wine itself

explanation.surface: Someone rescued by a supply of water and wine, like a traveller revived.
explanation.definitionFit: To be spared is to be let off or kept from harm, which is a common sense of rescued or preserved.

clue.text: Dump building outside

blocks.note: first meaning: to cast off or get rid of something
second meaning: a simple hut standing in the garden or yard

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a tip with a building outside it; the two halves are separate meanings, a verb and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means discard or cast off, as with leaves or skin; as a noun it is a small garden outbuilding.

clue.text: Did he deliver as US novelist?

blocks.note: first meaning: one who sends things out by post
second meaning: Norman ..., author of The Naked and the Dead

explanation.walkthrough: The question pretends to ask whether a writer delivered on his promise; the first sense is literally someone who sends post.
explanation.definitionFit: Norman Mailer was an American novelist, and the common noun describes a person or firm sending out post.

clue.text: One of those roasted in joke?

blocks.note: first meaning: a nut sold hot from braziers on winter streets
second meaning: a stale, overfamiliar gag told too often

explanation.surface: Someone being roasted, that is mocked, as part of a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roasted' hints at a comedy roast, but it means cooked over an open fire.
explanation.definitionFit: The edible nut is famously roasted on open fires, and an old chestnut is idiomatic for a tired, repeated gag.

clue.text: Asian individuals coming in from Kolkata, say?

indicators.note: people coming in enter a place, so one word goes inside another

blocks.note: Kolkata is a city in India, so a person from there is from that country
individuals are single units, ones

explanation.surface: Asian people arriving from Kolkata, as immigrants might.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Asian' and 'Kolkata' both point at India, but the answer is a different Asian nationality that merely contains the Indian one.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from the Southeast Asian archipelago nation centred on Java and Sumatra is, by geography, an Asian.

clue.text: Strike, touch careless

blocks.note: to slap is to strike with an open hand
a touch of something is a small amount, a dash

explanation.surface: A quick hit and a light touch, done without much care.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash work is hurried and sloppy, done without attention, which matches the adjective for lacking care.

clue.text: Equine sheep beyond a mix-up of characters!

indicators.note: beyond places the animal words after the article that comes before them

blocks.note: taken as written
a nag is a horse, an equine animal
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A farmyard jumble: a horse and sheep beyond something, with a jokey exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'beyond a' puts the animals below A, so A comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: A rearrangement of a word's letters into another word is exactly a jumbling of its characters.

clue.text: Capital invested in exotica, then squandered

indicators.note: money invested in something is put inside it, so the answer lies within the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: Money put into exotic goods and then wasted, a bad investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' and 'invested' make a finance story, but capital here is a city.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the chief city and seat of government of Greece, so it is a national capital.

clue.text: Peninsula in African country refusing leader

indicators.note: refusing the leader means turning away the first letter of the country's name

blocks.note: a West African country

explanation.surface: A peninsula inside an African nation that rejects its head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberia is the south-western European peninsula shared by Spain and Portugal.

clue.text: Fancy pants in use, old

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters that follow are a poor mess to be rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Fancy trousers still being worn even though they are old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy pants' reads as a phrase, but 'Fancy' is the definition and 'pants' (British slang for nonsense) is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy can be an idle fantasy or false belief, and a delusion is a mistaken belief held firmly.

clue.text: Spread margarine on, and fruit

indicators.note: spreading something moves it about, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to put margarine on bread, along with some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: This small loose-skinned citrus, related to the tangerine, is a fruit eaten fresh.

clue.text: A personal failing, with mistake finally admitted, for high-fliers

indicators.note: something failing breaks down, so the word's letters fall apart and rearrange
finally points to the last letter of the word it follows
admitted means let in, so that letter goes inside the jumbled word

blocks.note: taken as written
the letters to be rearranged
the final letter of mistake

explanation.surface: A private flaw, with an error owned up to, among high achievers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-fliers' suggests ambitious people, but it means the aircraft themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft travel at altitude, so they literally fly high; the 'for' introduces the plural definition.

clue.text: Specific taste of macaroni cheese

indicators.note: of here means made from, so the answer is formed from letters inside the next words

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A particular fondness for macaroni cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A niche is a specialised market or interest catering to a particular, narrow preference.

clue.text: Edge on front of bowler — that’s it!

definitions.text: Edge on front of bowler — that’s it!

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter
in an across clue, one part placed on another follows it

blocks.note: the first letter of bowler
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: Pointing out the edge at the front of a bowler hat: there it is!
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition, which 'that's it!' flags; a bowler is a round hard felt hat.
explanation.definitionFit: The projecting edge around a hat, such as a bowler, is called its brim.

clue.text: Soldier: I quit legion

blocks.note: a man is a soldier in the ranks
taken as written
to fold is to quit, as in giving up a hand at poker

explanation.surface: A soldier announcing that they are leaving the legion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legion' looks like a noun for an army unit, but it is the adjective meaning very many.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words, used as adjectives, describe something numerous or of great variety.

clue.text: Second hot drink, coffee

blocks.note: a mo is a moment, a second
cha is an informal word for tea

explanation.surface: A second hot drink, this one coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' looks like a separate H, but it belongs with 'drink' to describe tea.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a type of coffee, often blended with chocolate, named after the Yemeni port.

clue.text: A gang on leave

blocks.note: taken as written
a band is a group or gang
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gang going off on holiday leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leave' reads as a noun, time off, but it is the verb meaning desert.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon someone or something is to desert it, to go away and not return.

clue.text: Follow narrative on the radio?

indicators.note: on the radio things are only heard, so we go by the sound of the word

blocks.note: a narrative is a story or tale

explanation.surface: Keeping up with a story serialised on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: To tail someone is to shadow them secretly, keeping close behind as a detective might.

clue.text: Perilous arrival, something flipped onto floor at end of flight

indicators.note: onto here means the second part is joined directly after the first

blocks.note: a pancake is tossed in the pan to cook its other side
the level area at the top of a flight of stairs

explanation.surface: A dangerous landing: something flipped over, hitting the floor at the end of an aeroplane trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests air travel, but it is a flight of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an emergency touchdown where an aircraft drops flat onto the ground, often with its wheels up.

clue.text: Passionate office into music, for example

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the first word is placed within the second

blocks.note: music is an example of an art
a den is a private study or office

explanation.surface: Someone deeply keen on bringing music into the workplace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Office' is a private room here, the kind of study people call a den.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means fervent or burning with feeling, as an enthusiastic lover or supporter is.

clue.text: Fix pipe supplying water perhaps in field

blocks.note: to do something up is to fix or repair it
a main is a large supply pipe for water or gas

explanation.surface: A plumber repairing a water pipe running through a farmer's field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field' sounds like farmland, but it means an area of activity or knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words can mean a sphere of expertise or activity, such as an academic speciality.

clue.text: Flower father keeps out back, one ending in soil

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so the father's word surrounds the next part
back means the preceding word is read in the opposite direction
the ending of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: an informal word for father
off means out, as with a light switched out
I is the Roman numeral for one
the final letter of soil

explanation.surface: A father who keeps one flower outside, at the back, in the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: DA(FFO)D + I + L.
explanation.definitionFit: The daffodil is a yellow spring bloom of the narcissus family, so it is a flower.

clue.text: Fasten hair

blocks.note: first meaning: to secure a door with a key
second meaning: a tress or curl of hair

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an instruction to tie hair back; the two words are separate senses, a verb and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to secure something shut, and also a single curl or tress of hair from the head.

clue.text: Wanderer returned bearing small fruit

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards
bearing means carrying, so the word holds the next letter inside it

blocks.note: a nomad is a wanderer with no fixed home
S is the standard abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A wanderer comes back home carrying a little fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The word reversed gives DAMON, which then holds S: DAM(S)ON.
explanation.definitionFit: The damson is a small dark purple plum, a fruit often used in jams.

clue.text: River of Ukraine seems endless, initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so take the opening letter of each word

blocks.note: the first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A Ukrainian river that seems to go on forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' tempts you to drop a last letter, but it is just one of the words supplying an initial.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ouse is the name of several English rivers, including the one flowing through York.

clue.text: Old country only reforming after evacuation of Chile

indicators.note: evacuating something empties it, leaving only its outer letters
reforming means forming again in a different shape, so the letters are rearranged
after places the rearranged word behind the letters from the country

blocks.note: Chile with its middle emptied out
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A former nation that can only reform once Chile has been evacuated.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceylon was the colonial name for Sri Lanka until 1972, so it is a country under an old name.

clue.text: An insect on the move, most cautious

indicators.note: things on the move shift position, so the letters change their order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wary insect moving about, being as careful as it can.
explanation.definitionFit: Canny means shrewd and careful, especially with money, so its superlative is the most careful or shrewd.
